correctness.rationale: The Gaussian null line gives a quadratic exactly equivalent to RRR eigenvectors, and the smaller root modulus gives exact best sine angle. The small-root formula and root-product bound provide rigorous good/bad event estimates. Complex Gaussian squared moduli are unit-exponential: inverse-radius integrals yield the exact Pareto-2 limit, uniform p<2 moments, and E1(t) = -gamma-log t+O(t) at p=2. Gaussian logarithmic moments and fourth-moment bound control the remainder, proving the coefficient 1. The packaged checker confirms residual and angle algebra on actual sampled inputs; finite simulations are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with Shao (2026), including its existing deterministic Example 1 and RRR Theorem 2, isolates a new assertion: exact best-of-two Gaussian RRR sine-error Pareto moment spectrum and leading logarithmic L2 coefficient. Prior high-probability bounds with delta-dependent constants neither compute an expectation nor identify the finite-epsilon truncated denominator. Other retrieved results concern different eigenvector/sketch residual settings and do not imply this result. A complex Cauchy limiting ratio is classical and is not itself claimed novel; risk remains from specialized random-polynomial literature.

value.rationale: Expected squared sine-angle is a natural robustness criterion for randomized eigenvector extraction. The sharp oracle lower-bound risk epsilon² log(1/epsilon), compared to optimal subspace risk epsilon², quantifies an algorithmically meaningful loss invisible to fixed-confidence convergence statements. The full subcritical moment spectrum separates the convergent moment classes. It is not a mere restatement of the classical Gaussian-ratio law because the finite-epsilon quadratic two-root cutoff and constant are derived.
